text:
Emily Chen: Quick copy review  Confirmation modal for turning on Strict Structured Output (JSON schema enforcement) in the Playground/Console. Product wants the modal to warn about strict parsing failures but not scare users away. Current title: 'Enable strict structured output?' Body: 'Strict mode enforces a JSON schema and will reject non-conforming responses. Enable it?' Need tone + accessible wording.
Jordan Park: Prefer benefit-first. Title: 'Use strict structured output to enforce JSON responses' (maybe too long). Shorter: 'Turn on strict structured output?' In body call out the tradeoff in plain language: 'If the model returns malformed JSON it will be rejected; you can view parsing errors and fall back to non-strict mode.'
Samir Patel: UX nit: primary CTA should be explicit: 'Turn on strict mode' vs just 'Enable'. Secondary could be 'Learn more' (links to docs). Also include a small inline 'Examples' link that opens a modal with before/after outputs.
Olga Kuznetsova: Accessibility: modal should use role=dialog and focus the primary CTA. Don't use alarmist language. For screen readers, the CTA accessible name should include consequence: e.g., aria-label='Turn on strict mode; responses that do not match JSON schema will be rejected'. If we have a fallback option, include that in the body and aria-describedby.
Mei Tan: Research finding: devs liked 'strict' wording but non-dev PMs found 'reject' too scary. Suggest variants with 'validate' instead of 'reject' for friendly tone: 'Responses that don't match will be marked as invalid' vs 'rejected'.
Carlos Rivera: Implementation constraints: title field limited to 70 chars. Body: 300 chars. Mobile button truncation to 40 chars. i18n placeholder for schema name: `{{schema_name}}`. Need singular/plural handling for 'errors'.
Emily Chen: Draft copy options:
- Technical (concise): Title: 'Turn on strict structured output'
  Body: 'Strict mode enforces {{schema_name}}. Responses that do not match the schema are rejected and returned as parsing errors. You can switch back anytime.'
  Primary CTA: 'Turn on strict mode' (aria-label: 'Turn on strict structured output; parsing errors will be shown')
  Secondary: 'Learn more'
- Friendly (less scary): Title: 'Validate responses with structured output'
  Body: 'Strict mode validates responses against {{schema_name}}. Non-matching responses are shown as errors you can inspect; you can fall back to flexible mode at any time.'
  Primary CTA: 'Validate responses' (aria-label: 'Enable structured output validation, opens settings')
  Secondary: 'See examples'
- Minimal (banner/tooltip variant): 'Structured output: on' / Tooltip: 'Validates model output against {{schema_name}}. Click to change.'
Which should be default? A/B test tech vs friendly?
Jordan Park: A/B test Technical vs Friendly in the Console modal. For banners/tooltips always use Minimal. Also test CTA phrasing: 'Turn on' vs 'Validate' vs 'Enable' — devs prefer explicit verbs.
Samir Patel: UI note: show a small code sample under the modal body with a one-line example of a failure and success. Keep that collapsible on mobile.
Olga Kuznetsova: SR users: ensure the help link has rel=noopener and the modal's aria-describedby points to visible explanatory text. Avoid embedding long code blocks in the accessible name. Use a separate region with id for the code sample and link to it via aria-controls if opened.
Mei Tan: From research, 'Validate responses' increased perceived safety without reducing usage. Prefer Friendly copy for public docs, Technical for advanced settings toggles.
Carlos Rivera: Dev action: when schema is custom (user-provided), CTA should include 'for {{schema_name}}' if room allows, else present it in the body. Also add telemetry event when user toggles strict mode so we can measure reverts.
Emily Chen: Final suggested strings to land in PR (will include i18n keys):
- modal.title.tech = "Turn on strict structured output"
- modal.body.tech = "Strict mode enforces {{schema_name}}; responses that don't match the schema are rejected and returned as parsing errors. You can switch back anytime."
- modal.cta.primary.tech = "Turn on strict mode"
- modal.title.friendly = "Validate responses with structured output"
- modal.body.friendly = "Strict mode validates responses against {{schema_name}}. Non-matching responses are shown as inspectable errors; you can fall back to flexible mode at any time."
- modal.cta.primary.friendly = "Validate responses"
- banner.short = "Structured output: {{status}}"
Accessibility notes: Use role=dialog, focus trap, primary CTA gets focus; include aria-describedby pointing to full explanation; CTA aria-labels should use the full sentence from i18n key `{modal.cta.primary.aria}`.
design-bot: Saved copy variants and accessibility checklist. Task created DOCS-442 for examples page.
Samir Patel: I'll wire the collapsible examples and fallback switch. Please add string for 'Revert to flexible mode' for the secondary inline action.
Emily Chen: Will add that and push copy to the PR. Tagging @marketing for tone review and @security for any risks. :white_check_mark:
